rationale: The ground-truth thread's substantive asks were: don't let the model read cudagraph_mode (should be an upstream/runner concern), and flag that per-row seed reproducibility silently breaks under full cudagraphs for batch>1 needing a runner-side follow-up. X's comment #1 hits both directly, with a concrete alternative fix that moves the gating into the runner (exactly what the reviewers wanted) plus code showing the seed is discarded even for single-row replays — the sharpest and most grounded finding either candidate produced. Y treats the seed issue as already 'resolved' via the PR's own TODO and never engages with the architectural placement objection at all, so it recalls less of what reviewers actually cared about. Precision is close: Y shows more explicit verify/refute bookkeeping (a plus), while X reaches further into upstream vLLM internals (vllm/config/vllm.py, cuda_graph.py) that are harder to corroborate from the diff alone, but the two overlap heavily on secondary findings (prefix-caching/async-output conflict, stale yaml comments, duplicate assignment, capacity retune, missing tests), which corroborates both. X is marginally more actionable, offering inline suggested-diff code rather than prose-only asks.
